fatal_errors: The hypothesis substitutes an amorphous AlCrTiZrMo coating for the target as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic bulk alloy and omits the DS2205 comparator.
It replaces rapid 1100 °C heating/quenching and temperature-dependent testing in deionized water with a one-hour 800 °C oxidation treatment and testing in 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
The annealing comparison does not isolate the ZrTiO4 layer because annealing also changes microstructure, hardness, elastic modulus, and residual stress.
explanation: This is a scientifically plausible alternative supported by the cited AlCrTiZrMo-film paper, but it is not a reconstruction of the hidden target. It captures the general competition between sliding-induced depassivation and film repair, which overlaps with the target mechanism. However, it misses the target's central temperature-dependent transition from abrasion at 25 °C to minimum-wear polishing near 50 °C and oxide/third-body disruption at 100 °C, as well as the role of retained L12/B2 lamellae versus major phase redistribution in DS2205. Its predicted benefit of pre-oxidation is directionally supported by E1–E4, but the evidence attributes performance jointly to dense oxide, dense microstructure, and improved mechanical properties; it does not establish rapid regeneration of ZrTiO4 during sliding as the unique cause. The proposed in situ measurements could strengthen causal testing, yet the annealed-versus-as-deposited design remains confounded and the UHV control changes more than corrosion alone. Boundaries and a falsification rule are stated reasonably, although quantitative load, speed, and electrolyte limits are not supplied.
